ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, officer, authorized signatory, and material funder against the OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions schedules, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act regulations, Criminal Code terrorist entity lists, and FINTRAC's politically exposed persons (PEP) categories. Enhanced due diligence is required for domestic and foreign PEPs and their family members and close associates, including senior management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and ongoing real-time transaction monitoring. Screening is to be refreshed quarterly and upon any material ownership, control, or jurisdictional event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online — British Columbia Corporate Registry (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may use English or French legal elements; names in non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into a Roman-character English or French form and such transliteration must be set out in the notice of articles. A BC unlimited liability corporation must include a legal element such as 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC' at or at the end subject to the permitted position rules, and the name must not be contrary to public policy or confuse the public as to the entity's legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a proposed name under sections 20 through 29 of the BC Business Corporations Act, the applicant may submit a reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies through BC Corporate Online or via the BC Registry Services contact process, accompanied by written legal argument, evidence of prior use, marks distinguishing the name, and any consents from affected rights holders. If the Registrar sustains the refusal, the applicant may file an administrative appeal or application for judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 29, within applicable limitation periods, and should first obtain legal advice on the administrative remedies specific to the name decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if it is a real physical address in British Columbia used for registered office service and not a post office box; in practice this is satisfied by the office of a licensed registered agent. For an equity crowdfunding portal regulated by the British Columbia Securities Commission, the regulator will closely scrutinize whether there is genuine local management, personnel, books, and records; a bare virtual office without operational substance materially increases the risk of licensing refusal or delays.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 75.0% — unannounced physical inspection is considered likely within the first 12 months of portal licensing given the financial-intermediary classification, FINTRAC obligations, and BCSC compliance supervision.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c 57, ss. 10 (incorporation), 12 (memorandum), 13 (articles), 51 (directors), 88 (share capital)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Articles filed electronically through the BC Corporate Online service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a BC ULC may issue no-par share classes. Investor subscription funds for crowdfunding must be held in a trust/escrow account at an eligible Canadian bank under a written escrow agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for 1,000 no-par common shares is accepted, and the share ledger shall be updated accordingly. RESOLVED, that the registered office stated in the Notice of Articles is adopted, and the records office shall be maintained at that address. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed as Chief Executive Officer, Corporate Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, respectively, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED, that officers be directed to open escrow and operating bank accounts and adopt banking and corporate governance resolutions to facilitate the regulated equity crowdfunding business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry – Name Approval Process via NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete a corporate name request through BC Corporate Online or a licensed NUANS name search provider. Submit two or three alternative names for the ULC, including the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Review the preliminary search report for existing conflicts before proceeding with incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Written consent of any named individual or corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusion, choose a new distinctive element from the NUANS report or adopt a numbered company. A corrected name request may be resubmitted within 30 days without an additional search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles, Memorandum, and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry (drafting phase, filed electronically)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Notice of Articles, Memorandum, and Articles in accordance with the Business Corporations Act. Confirm the share structure, maximum number of shares, director provisions, and any optional special rights or restrictions. The incorporator and first directors must sign consent resolutions and any required director surety forms.
required_dossiers: Identification records for each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BC Registry queries a bylaw or share class provision, file amended Articles through the registry queue and pay the applicable notification fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application and Obtain Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online, British Columbia Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Notice of Articles, Memorandum, and Articles through BC Corporate Online. Pay the statutory filing fee. Upon approval, the registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation and stamps the Notice of Articles, constituting the ULC’s charter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is defective, the Registry returns a deficiency notice with a correction list; re-submit the corrected package in the same online queue, with no additional fee for the first correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute First Board Resolutions and Issue Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors of the company and corporate solicitor (registry update required after appointments)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written board consent. Adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Issue share certificates and update the share ledger and directors register, then file a Notice of Change of Directors/Officers with the BC Registry.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolutions or unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director fails to execute a consent in a timely manner, hold a valid board meeting within 10 days and ratify all prior actions by ordinary resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Federal and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the federally assigned Business Number to open CRA program accounts for GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll if employees are hired. Register with the BC Ministry of Finance for PST or employer health tax as applicable. Maintain the CRA account profile and appoint an authorized CRA representative.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is queried, contact the CRA Business Window with the certificate and BN notice; correct any mismatch in legal name or registered office and re-submit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as a Funding Portal (Restricted Dealer) under section 34 of the British Columbia Securities Act, RSBC 1996, c 418, and applicable crowdfunding exemption instruments

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office of British Columbia, Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt under Schedule A of the Environmental Assessment Act for a digital-intermediary office use; no industrial installation or physical emission source
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for an online equity crowdfunding portal. If a leased data center is used, applicable Metro Vancouver Air Quality Emissions Regulation and municipal sewer/stormwater discharge permits must be observed; no wastewater or VOC discharge is generated from the platform itself.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a municipal business licence, fire safety certificate from the local fire authority, building occupancy and structural load approval under the BC Building Code, and a WorkSafeBC workplace clearance or occupational health and safety registration for any physical office or data room.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) – Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; separate British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) registration via the BC Ministry of Finance eTaxBC portal. Federal and provincial tax administrations are not consolidated; GST/HST and income tax are administered by the CRA, while BC PST is administered provincially.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated ULC must first obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online and open an RT (GST/HST) program account, supplying certified constating documents (articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation or equivalent), registered office address, director and authorized signatory details, and, for non-resident registrants without a Canadian place of business, a Canadian-resident representative for service of notices and documents. The BC ULC must also register separately for PST through eTaxBC before taxable sales commence in British Columbia. Because the equity crowdfunding portal performs financial services, the non-resident issuer may additionally be required to register as a Selected Listed Financial Institution (SLFI) or, if applicable, qualify as an Isolated Financial Institution (IFI) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA). No minimum capital is prescribed. Public procurement of the BN and GST/HST account typically completes within 5–10 business days; PST registration is effective immediately online.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a BC-incorporated Unlimited Liability Corporation is deemed resident in Canada under Income Tax Act (ITA) s.250(4) and is taxed as a corporation at both federal and provincial levels on worldwide income; Canadian domestic law does not recognize pass-through treatment for a ULC notwithstanding its unlimited liability characteristics. Pass_Through_Eligible applies only for U.S. federal tax purposes if the entity makes a hybrid check-the-box election under IRC §7701, thereby becoming a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. tax while remaining a corporation for Canadian tax. No tax-exempt zone status is available.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian domestic check-the-box or entity classification election exists. Key available elections: (1) U.S. IRC §7701 check-the-box election via IRS Form 8832, allowing the ULC to be classified as a partnership or disregarded entity for U.S. federal tax purposes (hybrid planning); (2) voluntary GST/HST registration election for small suppliers under ETA s.242(1); (3) IFI election under ETA s.150 for a non-resident financial institution with nominal Canadian presence, allowing simplified GST/HST registration and recovery of input tax credits (ITCs); (4) annual GST/HST filing election for qualifying registrants under ETA s.238; and (5) appointment of a Canadian representative under ETA s.296.1 for non-resident registrants to ensure service of process. The ULC remains an entity-level taxpayer for Canadian corporate income tax purposes regardless of these elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST – federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) of 5%, administered by the CRA under the Excise Tax Act Part IX; British Columbia does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) and instead levies a separate retail Provincial Sales Tax (PST) of 7% administered by the BC Ministry of Finance. The combined nominal tax-inclusive burden on taxable goods and services in BC is 12%, but PST is not a value-added tax and is applied at point of sale on enumerated goods and certain services, with separate exemption and registration rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 – the small-supplier threshold under ETA s.148(1), measured on the basis of worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made by the entity, excluding supplies of capital property and financial services; a non-resident who makes no taxable supplies in Canada may nonetheless voluntarily register for GST/HST. Because the crowdfunding portal earns predominantly exempt financial-service fees (ETA Sch. V Pt. VII), such income does not trigger mandatory registration; however, any separate taxable supplies (e.g., marketing, data or technology services to Canadian customers) would count toward the $30,000 threshold. Once registered, the ULC must charge 5% GST on taxable (non-exempt) Canadian supplies and file returns on a fiscal-year basis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None – Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government digital stamping, or API-based e-invoice validation for private-sector invoicing. The CRA accepts electronically generated invoices (XML, EDI, PDF, PEPPOL BIS 3.0) provided they contain the prescribed information (ETA s.3 of Schedule V? No – information requirements under the ETA and the Input Tax Credit Information (GST/HST) Regulations). The federal Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework, based on PEPPOL and governed by the Digital Governance Council, becomes mandatory for federal B2G suppliers on a phased basis from April 2025 but does not apply to pure B2B equity crowdfunding invoices. All GST/HST registrants must file returns electronically (NETFILE, EDI, or GST/HST TELEFILE is discontinued) and remit payments via CRA My Payment or financial institution pre-authorized debit. Source records, including invoices and export documentation, must be retained for six years under ETA s.286(1).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exports applies under ETA Schedule VI. For goods, a supply is zero-rated if the supplier ships or delivers the tangible personal property to a destination outside Canada or exports it as soon as is reasonably possible after the consideration is due (ETA Sch. VI Pt. V s.5). For services other than financial services, a supply to a non-resident is zero-rated if it is for the non-resident's consumption or use wholly outside Canada (ETA Sch. VI Pt. V s.7). CRITICAL: the core fees of an equity crowdfunding portal – arranging the issue of shares or the provision of credit/financial intermediary services – are exempt financial services under ETA Schedule V Part VII (ss.1(a) and (d)), not zero-rated, and therefore do not attract GST but also confer no input tax credits on associated inputs. Zero-rating may only attach to clearly ancillary, non-financial services supplied to non-resident clients, such as specialized valuation, data hosting, or administrative back-office services, provided the non-resident consumption test is met and the service is not incidental to the exempt financial supply. Documentary evidence must demonstrate the recipient is a non-resident, the consideration is attributable to the qualifying supply, and the supply is not acquired for consumption in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed B13A Canada Customs Export Declaration filed through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS/CAED) or an alternative CBSA low-value export reporting record
Commercial invoice and the underlying crowdfunding service or securities placement agreement evidencing the nature of the supply, consideration and non-resident recipient
Bill of lading, international airway bill, or marine/rail waybill showing foreign destination and carrier receipt
CBSA export summary, carrier certificate of outward shipment, or customs broker confirmation of border clearance
Bank wire, SWIFT confirmation, or inward remittance record evidencing foreign-source consideration and, where applicable, FX conversion entry
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory 180-day export FX repatriation deadline under the Excise Tax Act; the 180-day field represents the administrative norm applied by CRA/CBSA for exports to be completed 'as soon as reasonably possible' and for transfer-pricing documentation. Delayed or unrealized repatriation can trigger CRA scrutiny under the transfer-pricing rules (ITA s.247) and, where funds are advanced to shareholders, a deemed shareholder loan under ITA s.15(2) if outstanding beyond one year. The CRA's normal reassessment period for GST/HST is four years under ETA s.298, extended indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect. Records supporting zero-rated exports must be maintained for six years (ETA s.286). Unsupported or fraudulent export zero-rating claims attract gross-negligence penalties equal to 25% of the net tax under-asserted (ETA s.280(1)), compound arrears interest at the prescribed rate (currently approximately 10% per annum), director and officer liability (ETA s.323), and criminal prosecution under ETA s.327(1), with fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Retrospective clawback operates by reassessment of the supply at 5% GST, plus BC PST if deemed supplied in BC, together with statutory interest and penalties, on a dollar-for-dollar recovery from the taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a current account convertibility regime with limited capital account controls. Resident corporations enjoy unrestricted convertibility for current account transactions, including profit remittances, subject to tax filing obligations and FINTRAC reporting. Capital account items such as portfolio investments require Bank of Canada notification in prescribed cases but present no convertibility barriers for bona fide commercial purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or prescribed conversion ratios apply to export receipts. Canadian residents may retain foreign currency proceeds in offshore accounts provided all transactions comply with FINTRAC reporting and applicable tax remittance requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility rating. Offshore digital EMIs are constrained by FINTRAC guidelines and AML requirements applicable to high-risk crowdfunding platforms; domestic banking rails remain the only compliant option.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening with video KYC verification is permitted for Canadian corporations. Directors may be required to attend physical interviews for enhanced due diligence in high-risk classifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk entity classification for equity crowdfunding platform
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, investor accreditation records, source-of-funds evidence, and proof of regulatory licensing
Corporate ownership chart, share percentages, and certified identification documents for all directors and shareholders

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital via domestic wire transfers or SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'EQTY' or 'CAPINV'. All transactions require full KYC/AML screening and documented purpose justification to FINTRAC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing through SWIFT MT103 for trade settlements or issuance of commercial letters of credit via correspondent banks. All outflows must reference verified trade contracts and pass AML screening.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act (S.B.C. 2002, c.57), section 270
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two calendar months after the anniversary of incorporation, continuation, or amalgamation in British Columbia; no fixed calendar date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is placed in default until filed; there is no separate statutory late charge in the BCA. If annual reports remain unfiled for two consecutive years, the Registrar may administratively dissolve the company; restoration requires a formal application and fee, and directors may incur liability for obligations arising after default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual funding-portal report and registrant annual renewal (Restricted Dealer -- Funding Portal) under the BC Securities Act, National Instrument 45-110, and National Instrument 31-103 registration requirements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Securities Commission (BCSC), filed through the National Registration Database (NRD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements and prescribed crowdfunding report due no later than 90 days after the portal's financial year-end (commonly December 31); NRD annual renewal must be completed within the BCSC-published renewal cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or renew results in suspension or cancellation of the funding-portal registration and a cease-trade or prohibition order preventing the portal from conducting equity crowdfunding distributions; reinstatement requires regulatory approval and payment of BCSC fee schedules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual transparency register confirmation and internal register audit under the BC Business Corporations Act (Part 9.1), recorded by shareholder consent or board resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records at the BC registered office; no submission to the Registrar of Companies is required in British Columbia.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuing obligation; confirmation at each fiscal year-end and within 15 days after any change in an individual with significant control or a share transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the BCA and may result in fines imposed by the court; it does not trigger administrative strike-off but exposes directors and officers to personal regulatory liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The BC Business Corporations Act does not impose an audit solely on private-company size thresholds for a non-reporting BC ULC. An independent audit becomes mandatory by regulatory condition because the entity is registered as a restricted-dealer funding portal under the BC Securities Act and NI 31-103; BCSC financial-statement requirements apply irrespective of revenue or assets. If the portal becomes a reporting issuer, additional NI 51-102 and audit-committee requirements apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Canada under CPA Canada Handbook Part I; ASPE (Part II) is Canadian GAAP and may be permitted only for a non-reporting issuer if accepted by the BCSC. IFRS is the prudent default for a BCSC-registered funding portal.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BC ULC is a private company and must maintain a Transparency Register identifying individuals with significant control. There is no annual UBO filing to the BC Registrar; the board and corporate secretary must review and confirm the register each fiscal year, record changes within 15 days of knowledge, and make the register available for lawful regulator and law-enforcement inspection at the registered office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200--USD 400 per year for a BC corporate-services agent providing registered office and records-maintenance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000--USD 18,000 per year for an independent CPA audit of a small funding-portal entity prepared under IFRS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined federal and British Columbia general corporate income tax (15% federal + 12% BC provincial)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 11% combined rate (9% federal + 2% BC small business) on the first CAD 500,000 of qualified active business income, available only if the unlimited liability corporation (ULC) qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC). A non-resident controlled ULC cannot claim the small business deduction. Additional incentives include investment tax credits under the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) program for qualifying research and development expenditures; no crowdfunding-sector preferential rate is legislated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically using Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) certified tax software via e-File/NETFILE; mandatory XML transmission applies to large corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than six (6) months after the end of the corporation’s fiscal period. The balance of tax payable is due no later than two (2) months after fiscal year-end, extended to three (3) months for CCPCs claiming the small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), registration number under the BC Business Corporations Act, and registered office address in British Columbia.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify all non-resident shareholders and attach the ownership schedule; update the CRA BN record to reflect the unlimited liability company structure and foreign controlling interest if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: End date of the tax fiscal period; the first fiscal period cannot exceed 53 weeks and may be selected to align with operating cycles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the fiscal period is consistently reported on all CRA and BC corporate registry filings; no separate fiscal period election is permitted for a non-resident controlled ULC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal taxable income computed after accounting for revenue, deductible expenses, loss carryovers, and adjustments under the Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A BC-incorporated ULC is resident in Canada and taxed on worldwide income; domestic transfer pricing and foreign accrual property income rules continue to apply to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 312 – Federal Part I Tax Before Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base federal corporate tax calculated at the 15% general rate on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim the small business deduction unless the corporation is a CCPC; a ULC majority-controlled by non-residents must instead apply the general rate and attach treaty-relevant schedules if claiming cross-border tax relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 4 – British Columbia Provincial Tax Calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax computed at 12% using allocation percentages for permanent establishments located in BC and other provinces.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine whether the ULC has a permanent establishment outside BC; file the schedule with supporting payroll and revenue allocation data to apportion taxable income among jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 88 – Transactions with Non-Arm’s Length Persons
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual schedule disclosing cross-border transactions with non-arm’s length persons, including platforms, escrow agents, and foreign affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File the schedule for every reportable transaction exceeding the applicable threshold; attach the local file, master file, and any advance pricing arrangement (APA) to substantiate the arm’s length price.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties include 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, with a repeat-failure additional 10% penalty. Knowingly filing false or misleading information is an indictable offense under the Criminal Code, punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 200% of evaded tax. Delinquent filing of Schedule 88/Form T106 attracts CAD 100 per day per information return, up to CAD 2,500 per return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, applied to all dividends paid or credited by a Canadian-resident corporation such as a BC ULC to non-residents of Canada.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete and deliver CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Treaty for Dividend Withholding) to the paying ULC before the dividend is paid, supported by a current Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. The ULC must withhold at the statutory rate in the absence of complete documentation. Under the Canada-United States Tax Treaty, a corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of voting shares is eligible for 5% withholding, and a portfolio corporate holder for 15%; other treaties may provide 0%, 10%, or 15%. Treaty benefits are denied if the Limitation on Benefits provision or a principal purpose test is failed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident are subject to a statutory 25% gross-basis withholding tax; treaty rates are generally 10% under the Canada-U.S. treaty, 0% for industrial royalties under certain domestic exemptions, and vary by jurisdiction. Interest paid to a non-resident is subject to a statutory 25% withholding, but treaty benefits frequently reduce this to 0% (e.g., Canada-U.S. treaty), except for participating debt interests or debt payable to non-arm's length parties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in aggregate related-party goods transactions and CAD 500,000 for related-party services, representing CRA administrative thresholds for mandatory contemporaneous documentation and filing of Form T106. No statutory safe-harbor threshold exists.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act, transfer pricing rules under section 247, controlled foreign corporation attribution rules, and the OECD BEPS Action Plan. A BC ULC operating an equity crowdfunding portal must demonstrate real board oversight, dedicated employees, office infrastructure, and the capacity to bear commercial risk; a shell-like ULC with no operational presence and nominal escrow arrangements will be re-characterized and may trigger GAAR, treaty override, or sham corporate veil-piercing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Failure to Report Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting platform fees, crowdfunding commissions, or escrow interest from taxable income in Canada or transferring revenue to a non-resident shell without arm’s length consideration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under section 239 of the Income Tax Act and section 380 of the Criminal Code; fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years on summary conviction or up to 14 years on indictment, plus assignment of interest and civil gross-negligence penalties under section 163.2.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unremitted source deductions and GST/HST under sections 227.1 and 323 of the Excise Tax Act; CRA may issue director’s liability assessments, freeze personal assets, prohibit international travel, and impose restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a BC ULC as a transparent pass-through vehicle for a US parent without proving commercial substance, or entering into circular subscription agreements to manufacture treaty eligibility for reduced dividend withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR permits reassessment to deny the tax benefit, add 25% Part XIII withholding on deemed dividends, assess penalty interest, and impose transfer pricing penalties under section 247. A sham transaction may be vitiated entirely, making all tax benefits void and subjecting the taxpayer to 100% gross negligence penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability under section 160 for transfers of property below fair market value to non-resident shareholders, and under section 227 for unpaid withholding taxes; significant infractions trigger criminal record and travel restrictions under court orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an equity crowdfunding portal without a registration or exemption under the BC Securities Act, or failing to implement anti-money laundering (AML) controls, including allowing anonymous high-value monetary transfers through non-compliant ACH escrow or wire rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the BC Securities Act, unregistered trading attracts administrative penalties up to CAD 5 million per occurrence and imprisonment up to 3 years; under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), failure to report suspicious transactions triggers penalties up to CAD 200,000 for individuals and CAD 1,000,000 for entities, plus the possibility of criminal prosecution for laundering proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for AML violations under the PCMLTFA and can be fined, debarred from securities registration, and held civilly liable to aggrieved investors for return of unlawfully solicited funds; in egregious cases, they face prison sentences up to 5 years and freezing orders on personal bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management fees, platform licence fees, or royalty-type charges to a related non-resident party to shift profits out of Canada, or failing to create contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation in connection with related party crowdfunding technology agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 247 of the Income Tax Act, CRA may reassess to adjust the transaction to an arm’s length price, impose a penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment, and add compound interest. Failure to file Form T106 or Schedule 88 yields daily penalties and, for intentional misconduct, gross negligence penalties up to 50% of the understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed to personal liability for unpaid corporate tax only if they sign a false certificate or receive a director’s liability assessment for payroll-type withholdings; however, in cross-border schemes, they may be personally sued for breach of fiduciary duty and subjected to CRA civil investigation, asset injunctions, and travel bans under the Criminal Code provisions.
